# dsh-todo-progress-guard
English | 中文

Gives the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) todo list a way to advance on its own: it nudges the model to
refre

sh `todo_write` during multi-step tool work, and completes stranded tasks when a turn ends
normally.
## The problem
DSH's `todo_write` replaces the whole list, and the list is only a session projection:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

So **the panel only changes when the model calls `todo_write` again**. Long tool-heavy turns show
tw
o familiar symptoms:
1. **Frozen mid-turn** — the model writes a plan once, then runs dozens of `bash` / `read` / `edit`

calls while its attention stays on tool output. The panel keeps showing the first item as
`in_progre

ss` for the rest of the turn.
2. **Stuck after the answer** — the model finishes the work and answer

s in a step with no tool
calls, so it never gets to send one last `todo_write`. The turn is over and

the panel still
reads `1 in progress · N pending`.

This bundle closes both gaps with one Host-side Cordis plugin. It changes no DSH core package and
in
vents no new session event types.
## Two mechanisms
### 1. Mid-turn reminder (`tools/post-execute`)

When the current turn owns an **incomplete** todo list and the model spends several steps or tool
ca

lls without calling `todo_write`, the plugin injects one context message
(`source.kind = "todo-progr

ess-reminder"`, `form: "notice"`, rendered as a collapsible injected row
in the chat stream) after t
he **last** tool result of that step.
The body repeats the current list verbatim, because `todo_write` replaces the whole list — the model
can copy it forward without re-reading distant history:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
### 2. Turn-end completion (`agent/turn-stopping`)

As a turn **ends normally** — before `turn/end` is written, while the turn is still legitimately
ope

n — any leftover `in_progress` / `pending` items are written back as `completed` through one final
`
todo/write` snapshot. The panel can never outlive the work it describes.
## Install

**The Web UI is the recommended path**: open **Plugins → Install** and paste any spec below.
It adds
the dependency *and* selects the bundle, so the patch applies immediately with no restart:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**The CLI only installs the package** (`dsh plugin` is a pnpm passthrough and does not select bundle
he CLI only installs the package** (`dsh plugin` is a pnpm passthrough and does not select bundles):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

After that, enable `dsh-todo-progress-guard` once in the Plugins page (equivalent to adding it to
`d

sh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/package.json`); only then is the bundle's
`cordis.pat

es` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<name>/package.json`); only then is the bundle's
`cordis.patch.yml` applied.
## Configuration

Defaults are usable as-is. To tune them, override this row's `config` by id in the profile's own
`co
rdis.patch.yml` (a patch layer replaces `config` wholesale, so restate all three keys):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `stepThreshold` | `2` | Remind after this many model steps without a `todo_write` |
| `callThresho
ld` | `5` | Remind after this many other tool calls without a `todo_write` (needs at least one step)

|
| `autoCompleteOnTurnEnd` | `true` | Complete leftover items when a turn ends normally |
The two thresholds are OR-ed: whichever is reached first reminds. At most one reminder per step, and
counters reset at every turn boundary. Invalid values (non-positive integers, non-booleans) fall ba

ck
to the defaults instead of failing activation.
## Safety boundaries
Completion only happens when the turn really did work. The plugin appends nothing when:

- the turn was aborted (`signal.aborted`) or the last assistant message was interrupted;
- a next st

ep is already queued (`agent.inbox.nextStep` is non-empty) — the turn is not over;
- the step called

`ask_user_question` or `exit_plan_mode` — the turn is waiting on a human, who
alone can decide whet
tool ran yet — that is a stated plan, not a result.
The plugin only **appends** `todo/write` events, never rewrites history, and always writes inside a

legitimately open turn, so it stays compatible with the durable-log invariants owned by
`@deepseek-a

turn, so it stays compatible with the durable-log invariants owned by
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo`.
## Compatibility

- Requires the Host `sessions` and `sessionProjections` services; the plugin stays inactive where
th

ey are absent (plain `inject` semantics) instead of failing the composition.
- Verified on DSH `0.2.

0-rc.2`. Every extension point it uses — `additionalContexts` on
`tools/post-execute`, `agent/turn-s

topping`, and the `todos` projection — is public contract there.
- **Zero runtime dependencies**: th

e plugin imports no DSH package, so a `link:` checkout and a
registry install behave identically. (E

xporting a Schemastery `Config` would break `link:`
installs, because a symlinked realpath cannot re

solve DSH packages; configuration is therefore
validated inside the plugin.)
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The tests drive the real plugin code through a minimal Host stand-in (session log + `todos`
projecti
on + tool waterfall) and import nothing from DSH.
